vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: withings-family
Version: 1.1.1

The skill is designed to interact with the Withings API to fetch health data for multiple family members. It implements standard OAuth flows, including a local callback server for automatic authentication. Key security considerations, such as sanitizing user IDs to prevent path traversal when storing token files (`tokens-<userId>.json`) and setting secure file permissions (`0o600`), are addressed. All network communication is directed to the legitimate Withings API endpoints or localhost for OAuth. There is no evidence of data exfiltration to unauthorized destinations, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts in the SKILL.md instructions. The code aligns with its stated purpose and includes reasonable security practices.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and required credentials align with its stated purpose (fetching Withings family health data); no unexpected network endpoints, installs, or unrelated secrets are requested.

dimensions.detail: Name/description ask for Withings data and the skill only requires WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET and python3 — all appropriate for OAuth and API calls to Withings. The included scripts call only Withings domains (account.withings.com, wbsapi.withings.net).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the included Python scripts, performing OAuth, and storing per-user token files under ~/.openclaw/withings-family (legacy ~/.moltbot). The runtime instructions and code operate within that scope and only read/write those token/config files. Minor documentation mismatches exist (SKILL.md mentions .env while code reads config.json; a docstring in oauth helper mentions port 8080 though code uses 18081), but these are documentation inconsistencies, not malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install step; this is instruction + Python scripts that use only the standard library. Required binary is python3, which is reasonable and expected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET are requested (client credentials required for OAuth). No unrelated secrets or broad environment/config paths are requested. Tokens are stored locally in the user's home directory with attempted chmod 600.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (not force-included). The skill stores per-user token files under its own directory and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. It runs only when invoked; autonomous invocation is allowed by default but not combined with other red flags.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it helps you fetch Withings data and uses OAuth to store per-user tokens in ~/.openclaw/withings-family (or legacy ~/.moltbot). Before installing, verify you trust the source repository, create a Withings developer app using the specified localhost callback URL, and set WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET in your environment. Inspect the tokens-<user>.json files if you want to confirm what's stored; the scripts attempt to set file permissions to 600. Note the minor doc mismatches (.env vs config.json, port docstring) and prefer the code's behavior when following setup steps.
